item.title: Bathroom Storage Without a Linen Closet: Where Towels and Toiletries Go
item.description: When a bathroom has no linen closet, it is tempting to add shelves until every spare towel and toiletry has a place. A small room then becomes harder to use: storage blocks the door, crowds the sink and leaves damp towels nowhere to dry. This guide separates what must be within reach from what only needs to be nearby, shows how to measure shelf spacing from your own folded towels and explains why medicines belong somewhere other than the bathroom cabinet.

item.title: Towel Storage for a Small Bathroom With No Wall Space
item.description: When a small bathroom has no free wall for a towel bar, the answer is usually not a bigger rack. It is a clearer split of jobs: a damp towel needs air and a place to hang open, while clean spares need a dry place to wait. Once those two needs have separate homes, the room gets easier to use. This guide starts with a towel count, then measures the door, the floor and the cabinet fronts before comparing options.
